title: Settings, Environment, and Tool Readiness Control Plane
goal: Make Settings the authoritative place for runtime readiness, tool availability, concurrency, integrations, AI provider status, scheduler behavior, and operator-safe configuration.
scope: Audit and improve Settings and readiness checks so every configurable field has bounds, examples, validation, saved-state feedback, and runtime effect. Add clear readiness cards for required pentest binaries, optional integrations, ChatGPT OAuth, scheduler, worker/inline dispatch mode, local concurrency limits, evidence storage, database encryption, threat intelligence cache, and live app health.
generation_reason: The operator needs settings that explain what can be entered and what it affects, including concurrency limits and tool availability. Earlier settings tasks added pieces, but not a unified readiness/control-plane view.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Settings/readiness only. Do not install tools automatically, bypass approvals, or change active assessment behavior except through existing persisted settings and documented runtime binding.

success_criteria: Settings exposes adjustable safe concurrency limits with min/max/default and explains runtime impact.
Tool readiness identifies installed/missing binaries and maps missing tools to affected assessment families.
Every Settings field has a label, placeholder/example, validation rule, and saved/error feedback.
ChatGPT OAuth status and reconnect behavior are clear and durable.
Threat intel, scheduler, integrations, database encryption, artifact storage, and host health show clear operational status.
Readiness output can be exported or attached to support/installation evidence.
out_of_scope: Installing tools as part of this task

required_checks: Focused Settings API tests for validation, bounds, persistence, and effective runtime settings
Browser tests for all Settings sections and readiness cards
acceptance_criteria: A new readiness artifact shows each runtime capability as ready, degraded, missing, or blocked with affected product behavior and operator next step.

before_promotion: backlog-153 has completed or been explicitly deferred by the operator.
after_completion: Promote exactly one next approved task into NEXT_TASK.md.
